doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Stock arrangements from a Dallas hotel band
summary: A white band at the Adolphus Hotel gave Albert's band a trunk of stock arrangements; Herman Waldman's band played the Baker Hotel.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well what sort of arrangements did you have for saxes? Well when we first started, they had Stockerman.
Because the band was formed so quickly. They had to have some music.

And there was a white band in Dallas Slain at the Adolphus Hotel. I can't remember the name of the screen so long ago. He said, well I'll tell you what I'm going to do. I'm going to bring you a stack of arrangements here tomorrow. And you can go ahead and arrest them. And the next day he brought them the whole trunk to all the arrangements.
And the priest started there. And later on, he started to have arrangements in the band.
He just gave them to you, didn't charge your compescent? Well he liked it.

He let them, and he heard. So he gave them some. It was there, Stock arrangements, about 40 or 50 cents. But when he was playing at the Adolphus, he'd get a lot of nothing. Just they were male-minded. Oh yeah. We'd have him play and he'd get duplicate copies.
He'd get a little duplicate copies. Hmm.
Did you tell me about Herman Wallman or something like that? Herman Wallman was the name of the city in San Antonio. Oh I see.
I just, I can't remember because it was...
Remember him all? Herman Wallman was the gunner.
Yeah, he played, he played a, the champ. The hotel, the Baker Hotel.
